content: 1. Ashrafizadeh M. conducted a study in 2021 to evaluate the impact of static stretching exercises on hip range of motion, pain levels, and disability in patients suffering from non-specific low back pain. The findings were published in the Journal of Experimental Orthopaedics. 2. Heidari RS, Sahebozamani M, and Karimi AF compared the effects of an 8-week core stability exercise program using a ball versus sling exercises on quality of life and pain in women with non-specific chronic low back pain. This study was published in the Journal of Zanjan University of Medical Sciences and Health Services in 2018. 3. Hemmati S, Rajabi R, Karimi N, and Jahandideh A investigated the effects of consecutive supervised core stability training on pain and disability in women with non-specific chronic low back pain. Their findings were published in Koomesh in 2011. 4. The World Health Organization (WHO) released guidelines for the non-surgical management of chronic primary low back pain in adults within primary and community care settings. 5. Idowu OA and Adeniyi AF conducted a randomized trial in 2020 to assess the efficacy of graded activity with and without daily-monitored walking on pain and back endurance in patients with concurrent low back pain and type-2 diabetes. The results were published in the Ethiopian Journal of Health Sciences. 6. Joseph LH, Hancharoenkul B, Sitilertpisan P, Pirunsan U, and Paungmali A compared the effects of massage combined with lumbopelvic stability exercises versus standard massage therapy in low back pain patients. This randomized crossover study was published in the International Journal of Therapeutic Massage and Bodywork in 2018. 7. Kanwal S, Yaqoob I, Shakil-ur-Rehman S, Ghous M, Ghazal J, and Namroz N conducted a comparative study in 2021 to evaluate the effects of core muscle stability on low back pain and quality of life in postmenopausal women. The findings were published in the Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association. 8. Karimi N, Talimkhani A, Mosallanezhad Z, Arab AM, and Keshavarz R studied the effects of consecutive supervised functional lumbar stabilizing exercises on postural balance and functional disability in low back pain patients. Their research was published in the Iranian Rehabilitation Journal in 2014. 9. Karimzadeh F, Ghasemi GA, and Letafatkar A examined the effects of an 8-week core stabilization exercise program on pain and functional disability in mothers of children with cerebral palsy. The study was published in the Scientific Journal of Kurdistan University of Medical Sciences in 2016. 10. Kell RT, Risi AD, and Barden JM explored the response of individuals with chronic non-specific low back pain to three different volumes of periodized musculoskeletal rehabilitation. Their findings were published in the Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research in 2011. 11. Kim S and Jee Y investigated the effects of 3D moving platform exercises on physiological parameters and pain in patients with chronic low back pain. The study was published in Medicina (Kaunas) in 2020. 12. Kim B and Yim J conducted a randomized controlled trial in 2020 to evaluate the impact of core stability and hip exercises on physical function and activity in patients with non-specific low back pain. The findings were published in the Tohoku Journal of Experimental Medicine. 13. Lang AE, Hendrick PA, Clay L, et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial in 2021 to assess the effects of an individualized pedometer-driven walking program on chronic low back pain. The study was published in BMC Musculoskeletal Disorders. 14. Li L and Feng Z observed the clinical effects of treating chronic non-specific low back pain with Baduanjin combined with sling exercise therapy. Their findings were published in Rheumatism and Arthritis in 2015. 15. Li Z, Yu Q, Luo H, et al. conducted a preliminary study in 2021 to evaluate the effects of virtual reality training on anticipatory postural adjustments in patients with chronic non-specific low back pain. The study was published in Neural Plasticity. 16. Liu J, Zhao W, and Yuan Y examined the effects of Tai Chi on event-related potentials in patients with chronic non-specific low back pain. Their findings were published in the Chinese Journal of Sports Medicine in 2018. 17. Liu J, Yeung A, Xiao T, et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial in 2019 to evaluate the effects of Chen-style Tai Chi on individuals aged 50 and above with chronic non-specific low back pain. The study was published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. 18. Madadi-Shad M, Jafarnezhadgero AA, Sheikhalizade H, and Dionisio VC studied the effects of a corrective exercise program on gait kinetics and muscle activities in older adults with low back pain and pronated feet. This double-blind randomized controlled trial was published in Gait & Posture in 2020. 19. McIlveen B and Robertson VJ conducted a randomized controlled study in 1998 to evaluate the outcomes of hydrotherapy for individuals with low back or back and leg pain. The findings were published in Physiotherapy. 20. Mendes PRF, Gomes SRA, Costa LDO, et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial in 2022 to assess the effects of core stabilization exercises on chronic low back pain in Air Force fighter pilots. The study was published in BMJ Military Health. 21. Noormohammadpour P, Kordi M, Mansournia MA, Akbari-Fakhrabadi M, and Kordi R evaluated the role of a multi-step core stability exercise program in treating nurses with chronic low back pain. This single-blinded randomized controlled trial was published in the Asian Spine Journal in 2018. 22. Park S, Park S, Min S, Kim C-J, and Jee Y-S conducted a randomized controlled trial in 2020 to investigate the effects of equine simulator riding on low back pain, morphological changes, and trunk musculature in elderly women. The study was published in Medicina. 23. The WHO released guidelines for the non-surgical management of chronic primary low back pain in adults within primary and community care settings. 24. Prado ERA, Meireles SM, Carvalho ACA, et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial in 2021 to evaluate the influence of isostretching on patients with chronic low back pain. The findings were published in Physiotherapy Theory and Practice. 25. Raoul T, Malfériot J, Barizien N, and Lhuissier FJ studied the effects of a spinal extensor muscle strengthening program in chronic low back pain triathletes. This randomized controlled study was published in the Journal de Traumatologie du Sport in 2019. 26. Rathi M investigated the effects of pelvic floor muscle strengthening exercises on chronic low back pain. The findings were published in the Indian Journal of Physiotherapy and Occupational Therapy in 2013. 27. Raza S, Awan WA, Ghauri MW, et al. evaluated the effectiveness of spinal stabilization exercises with and without stretching of the latissimus dorsi muscle in chronic mechanical low back pain. The study was published in the Rawal Medical Journal in 2020. 28. Sedaghati P, Ardjmand A, and Sedaghati N compared the effects of different training approaches on dynamic balance and pain intensity in patients with chronic back pain. The findings were published in the Scientific Journal of Kurdistan University of Medical Sciences in 2017. 29. Shariat A, Alizadeh R, Moradi V, et al. conducted a randomized clinical trial in 2019 to assess the impact of modified exercise and relaxation therapy on chronic lower back pain in office workers. The study was published in the Journal of Exercise Rehabilitation. 30. Shu J, Li D, Tao W, and Chen S observed the curative effects of massage manipulation combined with core strength training in patients with chronic non-specific low back pain. The findings were published in Evidence-Based Complementary and Alternative Medicine in 2021. 31. Sokhangoi Y, Noorabadi MH, and Noorabadi MS studied the effects of Pilates exercises on chronic non-specific low back pain and stable range of motion in women aged 40 to 60 years. The findings were published in the Scientific Research Journal of Zanjan University of Medical Sciences in 2017. 32. Srivastav N, Joshi S, and Kushwah SS compared the effectiveness of lumbar stabilization exercises and conventional physical therapy in managing mechanical low back pain. The study was published in the Indian Journal of Physiotherapy and Occupational Therapy in 2018. 33. Suh JH, Kim H, Jung GP, et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial in 2019 to evaluate the effects of lumbar stabilization and walking exercises on chronic low back pain. The findings were published in Medicine (Baltimore). 34. Wattamwar RB and Nadkarni K studied the effects of conventional occupational therapy and yoga on chronic low back pain. The findings were published in the Indian Journal of Occupational Therapy in 2012. 35. Xu C, Fu Z, and Wang X evaluated the effects of transversus abdominis muscle training on pressure-pain threshold in patients with chronic low back pain. The study was published in BMC Sports Science, Medicine, and Rehabilitation in 2021. 36. Yalfani A, Abedi M, and Raeisi Z conducted a double-blind randomized clinical trial in 2022 to assess the effects of an 8-week virtual reality training program on pain, fall risk, and quality of life in elderly women with chronic low back pain. The study was published in Games for Health Journal. 37. Zadro JR, Shirley D, Simic M, et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial in 2019 to evaluate video-game-based exercises for older individuals with chronic low back pain. The study was published in Physical Therapy. 38. Zakari UU, Bello B, Sokumbi GO, et al. compared the effects of positional release therapy and lumbar stabilization exercises in managing chronic mechanical low back pain. The findings were published in Critical Reviews in Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine in 2019. 39. Brinkhaus B, Witt CM, Jena S, et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial in 2006 to evaluate acupuncture in patients with chronic low back pain. The study was published in the Archives of Internal Medicine. 40. Cherkin DC, Sherman KJ, Avins AL, et al. compared acupuncture, simulated acupuncture, and usual care for chronic low back pain in a randomized trial published in the Archives of Internal Medicine in 2009. 41. Cho YJ, Song YK, Cha YY, et al. conducted a multicenter, randomized, patient-assessor-blind, sham-controlled clinical trial in 2013 to evaluate acupuncture for chronic low back pain. The study was published in Spine. 42. De Castro Moura C, Chaves ECL, Chianca TCM, et al. evaluated the contribution of Chinese and French ear acupuncture for managing chronic back pain in a randomized controlled trial published in the Journal of Clinical Nursing in 2019. 43. De Paoli Lemos VJ, Selau RC, Blos C, et al. studied the effects of electroacupuncture and transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation in chronic non-specific low back pain in a blinded randomized clinical trial published in Muscles, Ligaments, and Tendons Journal in 2021. 44. Haake M, Muller HH, Schade-Brittinger C, et al. conducted the German Acupuncture Trials (GERAC) for chronic low back pain, a randomized, multicenter, blinded, parallel-group trial published in the Archives of Internal Medicine in 2007. 45. Huang Z, Liu S, Zhou J, et al. evaluated the efficacy and safety of acupuncture for chronic discogenic sciatica in a randomized controlled sham acupuncture trial published in Pain Medicine in 2019. 46. Kerr DP, Walsh DM, and Baxter D conducted a blinded randomized controlled trial in 2003 to evaluate acupuncture in managing chronic low back pain. The study was published in the Clinical Journal of Pain. 47. Kim H, Mawla I, Lee J, et al. linked reduced tactile acuity in chronic low back pain to structural neuroplasticity in the primary somatosensory cortex, modulated by acupuncture therapy. The findings were published in NeuroImage in 2020. 48. Kong JT, Puetz C, Tian L, et al. conducted a randomized clinical trial in 2020 to compare the effects of electroacupuncture versus sham treatment on pain severity in adults with chronic low back pain. The study was published in JAMA Network Open. 49. Li SK, Zhao J, Cao XW, et al. studied the effects of core stability training combined with acupuncture in treating chronic non-specific low back pain in a prospective randomized controlled trial published in Zhen Ci Yan Jiu in 2022. 50. Li YJ, Zhuang WS, Cai XG, et al. evaluated the effects of acupuncture at three points of ilio-lumbar on lumbar function and pain in patients with iliopsoas muscle strain. The study was published in Zhongguo Zhen Jiu in 2019. 51. Martín-Corrales C, Bautista IV, Méndez-Mera JE, et al. assessed the benefits of adding gluteal dry needling to a four-week physical exercise program in a chronic low back pain population. The study was published in Pain Medicine in 2020. 52. Meng CF, Wang D, Ngeow J, et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial in 2003 to evaluate acupuncture for chronic low back pain in older patients. The study was published in Rheumatology (Oxford). 53. Molsberger AF, Mau J, Pawelec DB, et al. conducted a randomized, blinded, controlled trial in 2002 to evaluate acupuncture's role in orthopedic management of chronic low back pain. The study was published in Pain. 54. Moslemi F and Farokhi ZS studied the effects of electroacupuncture on pain, functional disability, and ultrasonographic changes of the gluteus maximus muscle in non-specific chronic low back pain patients with gluteus maximus muscle trigger points. The findings were published in Koomesh in 2020. 55. Pan J, Yang L, Qiu Y, et al. evaluated the clinical effects of acupuncture combined with sling exercise training on lumbar disc herniation. The study was published in the Journal of New Chinese Medicine in 2019. 56. Ran P studied the effects of acupuncture on pain and lumbar function in patients with discogenic low back pain. The findings were published in the Clinical Journal of Traditional Chinese Medicine in 2021. 57. Ren B, Feng X, and Zhang C evaluated the analgesic effects of acupuncture based on meridian-tendon dialectical theory in chronic low back pain. The study was published in the Chinese Journal of Rehabilitation Medicine in 2021. 58. Shi F, Dong B, Lin X, and Fu Y observed the treatment effects of non-specific low back pain based on meridian theory and acupuncture. The findings were published in the Journal of Practical Traditional Chinese Internal Medicine in 2021. 59. Sung WS, Hong Y, Jeon SR, et al. conducted a randomized, controlled, assessor-blinded, multicenter clinical trial in 2020 to evaluate the efficacy and safety of thread embedding acupuncture combined with acupuncture for chronic low back pain. The study was published in Medicine. 60. Tabatabaiee A, Takamjani IE, Sarrafzadeh J, et al. evaluated the effects of ultrasound-guided dry needling on pain in patients with piriformis syndrome. The findings were published in Muscle & Nerve in 2019. 61. Ushinohama A, Cunha BP, Costa LO, et al. studied the effects of a single session of ear acupuncture on pain intensity and postural control in individuals with chronic low back pain. The findings were published in the Brazilian Journal of Physical Therapy in 2016. 62. Wang L, Wang Z, Wang Y, and Guo Y observed the efficacy of acupuncture for lumbar intervertebral disc herniation. The study was published in the Shanghai Journal of Acu-Mox in 2020. 63. Wang X, Yu X, Huang F, et al. evaluated the effects of acupuncture combined with fire acupuncture on pain and serum inflammatory factors in patients with lumbar disc herniation. The findings were published in a Chinese medical journal.
